description:
Welcome to our team! We are working on the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge for NASA Space Apps 2026.

Our goal is to design an interactive and engaging game/simulation app that teaches students how to balance life support, power, radiation shielding, and food production for a lunar or Martian outpost.

If you are interested in space, game design, or coding, feel free to join us!
summary:
**Artemis Lunar Survival – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer**

Artemis Lunar Survival is an interactive, browser-based space survival simulation designed to introduce young learners to the real challenges of human exploration on the Moon.

The project places players in the role of lunar mission planners and challenges them to keep astronauts alive by managing essential resources, including oxygen, water, food, solar power, and fuel. Through a five-stage mission experience, players encounter realistic survival scenarios involving pre-launch preparation, resource management, equipment failures, lunar agriculture, and emergency resupply and extraction.

Developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, the simulation transforms complex space engineering concepts into interactive decision-making experiences. Inspired by NASA's Artemis exploration principles, lunar In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU), and space agriculture research, the project demonstrates how engineering decisions affect astronaut survival.

Our goal is to make space exploration more accessible, engaging, and educational while helping young learners understand that surviving beyond Earth requires planning, teamwork, innovation, and responsible resource management.
details:
Project Details

1. Project Overview

Artemis Lunar Survival is an interactive, browser-based survival simulation that demonstrates the challenges astronauts may face while establishing a sustainable human presence on the Moon. Players take responsibility for mission planning, resource allocation, lunar surface operations, and crew survival.

The experience is designed around five mission stages, transforming important space exploration concepts into practical challenges that players can understand through gameplay.

2. How the Project Works

The simulation includes the following mission stages and systems:

Stage 1 – Pre-Launch Mission Control

  • Players prepare their lunar mission by managing eight essential systems: oxygen, food, water, power, fuel, cargo, health, and mission duration.
  • Every adjustment creates a trade-off that affects overall mission readiness.
  • Players can simulate critical failures, including oxygen leaks, fuel leaks, solar flares, and power overloads.

Stage 2 and Stage 3 – Mission Survival Operations

  • Players progress through the lunar survival mission and face operational challenges.
  • Mission decisions require balancing available resources and responding to changing survival conditions.

Stage 4 – Lunar Surface Greenhouse

  • Players cultivate crops using lunar water ice and LED grow lights.
  • The objective is to maintain food production during a simulated 120-day period without new food supplies.

Stage 5 – Resupply and Extraction

  • Players align a high-gain communication dish with the Lunar Gateway.
  • They clear dust from the landing area and transmit the final landing beacon to guide the rescue spacecraft.

3. Key Features and Benefits

  • Interactive five-stage lunar survival experience.
  • Resource management involving oxygen, water, food, solar power, and fuel.
  • Mission readiness monitoring and resource trade-offs.
  • Emergency failure simulations.
  • Lunar greenhouse and sustainable food production.
  • Communication, resupply, and astronaut extraction challenges.
  • Browser-based accessibility without requiring specialized hardware.

4. NASA Science and Educational Impact

The project draws inspiration from NASA's Artemis lunar exploration principles, In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU), and space agriculture research.

It introduces players to the concept of using local lunar resources rather than depending entirely on supplies transported from Earth. It also demonstrates why resource conservation, recycling, sustainable food production, and reliable communication are essential for future lunar missions.

The intended impact is to make space science understandable and engaging while developing critical thinking, problem-solving, and resource-management skills.

5. Development Tools and Technologies

The project is developed using:

  • HTML – Webpage structure and game interface.
  • CSS – Visual design, layout, and styling.
  • JavaScript – Gameplay mechanics, interactions, resource management, and mission logic.
  • Antigravity – Development environment, if used in the final implementation.

6. Creativity and Innovation

The project combines space education with survival-style gameplay. Instead of simply presenting facts about lunar exploration, it allows players to experience the consequences of mission decisions.

Its interactive mission-control dashboard, emergency simulations, lunar agriculture, and final extraction challenge create an engaging learning experience inspired by the engineering principles behind sustainable space exploration.
